items.title: Fooled twice: People cannot detect deepfakes but think they can

judge.evidence_empirical: In a pre-registered behavioral experiment ( N = 210), we show that (a) people cannot reliably detect deepfakes, and (b) neither raising awareness nor introducing financial incentives improves their detection accuracy.
judge.evidence_topic: Hyper-realistic manipulation of audio-visual content, i.e., deepfakes, presents a new challenge for establishing veracity of online content. Research on the human impact of deepfakes, addressing both behaviors in response to and cognitive processing of deepfakes, remains sparse.
judge.reason: O resumo trata de deepfakes e da capacidade humana de detectá-los, dentro do recorte de estudo empírico com participantes humanos. O experimento é pré-registrado, descrito com os mesmos métodos extraídos (conscientização e incentivos financeiros), e o achado reflete precisamente os resultados do resumo: pessoas não detectam deepfakes de forma confiável, confundem deepfakes com vídeos autênticos e superestimam suas habilidades.

items.title: Warning: Humans cannot reliably detect speech deepfakes

judge.evidence_empirical: We presented genuine and deepfake audio to n = 529 individuals and asked them to identify the deepfakes.
judge.evidence_topic: Speech deepfakes are artificial voices generated by machine learning models. We presented genuine and deepfake audio to n = 529 individuals and asked them to identify the deepfakes.
judge.reason: O achado extraído (capacidade de detecção pouco confiável, 73% de acertos, sem diferença entre inglês e mandarim) é exatamente o que o resumo relata: 'detection capability is unreliable. Listeners only correctly spotted the deepfakes 73% of the time, and there was no difference in detectability between the two languages.' O método descrito confere com o resumo, e o estudo é empírico com participantes humanos, no tópico de detecção de deepfakes de áudio por pessoas.

items.title: Deepfake detection by human crowds, machines, and machine-informed crowds

judge.evidence_empirical: In two online studies with 15,016 participants, we present authentic videos and deepfakes and ask participants to identify which is which.
judge.evidence_topic: In two online studies with 15,016 participants, we present authentic videos and deepfakes and ask participants to identify which is which.
judge.reason: O achado principal está totalmente sustentado pelo resumo. O resumo afirma que observadores humanos e o modelo tiveram precisão semelhante e cometeram erros diferentes ('we find them similarly accurate, while making different kinds of mistakes'), e que manipulações que perturbam o processamento visual de rostos prejudicaram os humanos ('manipulations designed to disrupt visual processing of faces hinder human participants’ performance while mostly not affecting the model’s performance').

judge.evidence_topic: Here we investigate the impact of the belief that depicted persons are real or deepfakes on psychological and neural measures of human face perception.
judge.reason: O artigo investiga como a crença de que rostos são deepfakes afeta a percepção e avaliação emocional em participantes humanos, alinhando-se ao tema de percepção de imagens sintéticas. É um estudo empírico com EEG e julgamentos, e o método extraído corresponde ao resumo. O achado principal é integralmente sustentado pelo resumo, que relata menor positividade e redução do processamento para sorrisos tidos como deepfake, mas não para expressões de raiva.
